evidence_refs.detail: 26 untracked files across four directories of Discovery-skill scaffolding and QA fixtures for unrelated fictitious applications were found inside the application source tree, flagged independently by five passes as an upstream staging defect.

options.label: Accept the scope — this application does belong in the portfolio
options.description: Confirms the application is correctly assigned and this Discovery package may be consumed as scoped. You are also accepting that FAA-specific gating has no basis in the application's own content, so safety tiering, NAS impact assessment and compliance mapping must be driven by stakeholder input rather than by evidence from this package. The profile owner should then add a classification path for non-aviation administrative systems and a modernization target for the VB.NET WinForms plus Access stack, neither of which exists today.

options.label: Rescope — the wrong application or the wrong profile was staged
options.description: Halts consumption of this package and returns the application to onboarding. All 36 synthesized findings, the criticality rating and the SRS remain valid descriptions of the repository that was analysed, but they do not describe whatever application was intended to occupy this portfolio slot, and they must not be carried forward against it. Given that Discovery-skill scaffolding and unrelated QA fixtures were found staged inside the source tree, a staging error is a live possibility worth checking first.

review_asks.title: For the record: what this Discovery synthesis found, and what it could not settle
review_asks.why: A reviewer needs to know what the synthesis was built from and what it deliberately left open, so that retained uncertainty reads as honesty rather than as an oversight.

confidence.rationale: Ten Discovery passes were present and consumed, and the two recorded as not-applicable self-declare that status in their own text. The merge is keyed on a structural spine of six modules whose identifiers are used consistently by every pass that references a module, so the join is exact rather than fuzzy. Confidence is held below the mid-nineties because thirteen open questions remain and the scope question above is unresolved.

review_asks.assessment: Ten Discovery passes were available and all ten were consumed: catalog, structural analysis and its .NET specialist, business rules, quality and risk, UX and accessibility, data domains, shared database, capability, and compliance citations. Two further specialist passes were emitted by the pipeline but do not apply to this application by subject — a document-imaging corpus assessment for an application with no images, and a SQL Server inventory for an application that uses Microsoft Access — and both say so themselves; they are recorded as not-applicable rather than scored. No expected pass was missing, so nothing in this synthesis rests on an unexplained gap. From those inputs we consolidated 36 findings: 16 at high confidence because two or more passes confirmed them independently, 12 at medium, and 8 deliberately retained at low confidence as known-unknowns. Twenty-five of the 36 are flagged as needing a target-architecture decision. We also recorded 12 genuine disagreements between passes, each with both claims preserved and an explicit reconciliation, and routed 13 open questions to the domain areas that can answer them. One of those is blocking: whether this is the right application at all. The headline technical picture is a structurally simple application with a serious security and data-governance posture — no authentication anywhere, a live SQL-injection path, student personal data in a public repository, zero accessibility annotations against a Section 508 obligation, no tests and no externalized configuration — while the measured data payload is two rows.
review_asks.reasoning: The merge was keyed on the structural pass's six module identifiers, which every other pass that references a module uses verbatim, so the join is exact. Findings were promoted to high confidence only where passes reached the same conclusion by independent means — for example the injection path was found by a structural walk, re-verified by a separate source read, recorded as a code smell, and independently flagged by the .NET specialist, all at the same file and line. Contradictions were resolved in favour of the better-evidenced pass where one clearly was better evidenced, reconciled by distinguishing scope where both were right about different things, and left open where neither dominated; in no case was a losing claim deleted. Two of the twelve are not disagreements about the application at all but defects in the pipeline — a capability pass that ran before its required input existed, and a vulnerabilities field left empty in an artifact that reports a confirmed exploitable injection elsewhere in the same document — and both are routed upstream because a consumer reading either field in isolation would be misled.

evidence_refs.name: Input completeness: ten passes present, two not applicable by subject
evidence_refs.detail: Recorded row by row in input_inventory, with the justification for each not-applicable classification stated from the subject's own evidence rather than from an assumption about the pipeline.

evidence_refs.name: 36 consolidated findings, 25 architecturally significant
evidence_refs.detail: 16 high confidence (cross-pass confirmed), 12 medium (single pass with strong evidence), 8 low (retained known-unknowns). The 25 flagged architecturally significant are the ADR-coverage denominator for the Architecture line and must not be re-scored downstream.

evidence_refs.name: 12 cross-pass contradictions, both claims preserved
evidence_refs.detail: Includes two pipeline defects visible only at synthesis: a capability pass that ran before the data-domain input it requires, and an empty vulnerabilities array in an artifact whose own risk summary reports a confirmed exploitable SQL injection.

evidence_refs.name: Escalation ESC-1 remains open and is routed independently
evidence_refs.detail: Student personal data committed to a public repository with no database password, no application authentication and a confirmed injection path. Routed to a named data-protection owner as OQ-005, deliberately decoupled from modernization sequencing.
